doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recovering from the stroke, helped by Randy
summary: After the stroke one must relearn everything; Randy and her mother pushed her and Randy got her writing again.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You got to turn [?] loose. But what did you think after you had your stroke? What did you think? Did you think you would be able to play again? What?
You don’t think. It’s a long time before you can think. You learn how to eat with . . .
It’s the learning process all over?
Yeah, but I think Randy pushed me along.
Before you even – before you came out here?
But when you got here, your mother was still alive. Did she push you too?
Oh yeah, but Randy helped me to get started writing, and so I’m doing it. I’m not writing as fast and all of that as I . . .
The quality is there though, Melba.
. . . I used to, but maybe I’ll get that back in New York, but I don’t have to go as fast, anyway.
